The '''constitution''' outlines the fundamental principles of a [[legal system]].<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>

A modern constitution often:

* confirms fundamental [[human rights]],
* proclaims the basis of legitimacy of itself and other laws,
* dictates the organisation of the government,
* specifies what other laws can and should be enacted.

== The Supreme law ==

In most [[jurisdiction]]s, the constitution is '''supreme''': i.e., no other law can contradict it.
